newsitem.title: CHINA: North, South Korean Red Cross fail to reach accord.
newsitem.headline: North, South Korean Red Cross fail to reach accord.

text.p: Negotiators from the Red Cross organisations in North and South Korea failed on Monday to reach agreement on shipments of grain aid to the hungry and isolated North, South Korean officials said.
"In today's meetings we did not get a final agreement between the two sides," Lee Byung-Woong, secretary general of the South Korean Red Cross told reporters.
However, talks would resume through a direct telephone line in the Korean border town of Panmunjom, he said.

The talks stalled over the exact method of delivery for the grain to the North. The South insisted on channels for direct shipments while the North opposed that formula and wanted a pledge of an exact aid amount before it could agree to anything, Lee said.
"We suggested a meeting to discuss the method of delivery," Lee said. "The North Korean Red Cross side insisted if we show an exact amount of an assistance, then they can discuss other issues."
The talks on speeding up food aid to the hungry North began on Friday, the first such inter-Korean Red Cross talks in almost five years.
